name: Louisiana
overview: Under the law in effect since January 1, 2026, Louisiana parish tax collectors auction tax lien certificates on immovable property with unpaid taxes; the property itself is not sold at the auction. The parish tax collector advertises the auction on or before May 1 of the year after the taxes were assessed, and the auction may be held on any weekday. Bidding is competitive on the interest rate: bids start at a maximum of one percent per month and bidders bid the monthly rate down. The state constitution requires a period during which the lien cannot be enforced, giving the owner time to pay before the certificate holder can act.

overview_sources.quote: The tax collector shall advertise for sale by public auction the tax lien
on or before May first of the year following the year in which the taxes were assessed
The tax lien auction shall be conducted on any weekday, with bidding opening not earlier than 8:00 a.m.
Subject to a maximum bid of one percent per month, bidders may submit bids reducing the monthly interest rate
(c) A period of time during which the lien cannot be enforced.

counties.how_to_bid: Bidders must register online in advance; registration dates are advertised for each tax year. The Sheriff calls the sale a 'buyer beware' environment. Deposit: not stated.
